key_insight: Sharing activation candidates across periods and evaluating schedule completion improves recovery of low-activation, switching-constrained D-FACTS schedules regardless of candidate source.
engineering_relevance: The approach helps allocate limited physical checks when scheduling grid moving target defense under operating and device-switching constraints.
method: Generate activation candidates with QAOA or classical alternatives.
Share candidates across periods and prioritize checks using schedule-completion evaluation.
Use classical scheduling to enforce operating and switching constraints.
evidence_signal: In a modified IEEE 118-bus study, combined checking improved final-budget reference-objective recovery for every tested generator in the primary operating window, with identical recovery curves for quantum and classical candidates.
watch_item: Results are limited to the evaluated candidate set and operating windows and do not establish a quantum advantage.
paper_title: Quantum-Assisted D-FACTS Scheduling for Moving Target Defense under Switching Limits
